THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED: 16/02/2018,
PASSED IN MVC NO.1073/2016, ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC., AND ADDITIONAL MACT, HIRIYUR,
AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.16,82,294/- ALONG WITH INTEREST AT 7.5% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT
1. The insurer as well as the claimant are in appeal challenging the compensation awarded and the apportionment of liability.
2. The accident occurred on 21.01.2016 when the claimant was riding a motorcycle and was hit by another motorcycle.

As a result of this accident, the claimant suffered grievous injuries and was taken to the Government Hospital, Hiriyur and thereafter, admitted to NIMHANS and ultimately,
treated at Manipal Hospital, Bangalore.
The claimant thereafter preferred a claim petition which has been accepted and the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.16,82,294/- as compensation.
4. Being aggrieved, both the insurer as well as the claimant are in appeal.

5. The insurer contends that the accident itself was doubtful since the Wound Certificate issued by the Government Hospital merely states history of a road traffic accident without mentioning the date etc., and therefore, the occurrence of the accident involving the vehicle that it had insured cannot be believed.
6. It is noticed here that in the Wound Certificate issued by the Government Hospital, there is a mentioning of history of a road traffic accident.

The claimant has also produced the Emergency Case Record of NIMHANS which also contains a note of a history of a road traffic accident between two 2-wheelers, i.e., when a two wheeler hit another two wheeler and the NC: 2024:KHC:50808 claimant had altered sensorium with history of vomiting.

7. Ultimately, the claimant was taken to Manipal Hospital where he was admitted on 22.01.2016 and The Branch Manager vs Veluswamy on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21297794/
3 discharged on 23.02.2016.

sentences.text: In my view, in light of these three medical records which indicate an accident between a two wheeler and the immediate admission of the claimant to the hospital, the assertion of the claimant that an accident occurred between his two wheeler and the another two wheeler cannot be denied.

The police have, in fact, investigated the case and laid a charge-sheet against the rider of the offending motor-cycle and this also points to the fact that the two wheeler insured by the insurer was involved in the accident.

10. Further, the motor vehicle inspection report produced also indicates extensive damages to both the motorcycles and this would also therefore clearly establish that an accident occurred between two motorcycles.
11. In light of these facts, there is no merit in the argument of the insurer that the accident was doubtful.
12. As far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the claimant examined the doctor as PW-2 who has re-iterated the multiple fractures suffered by the claimant.
He has ultimately stated that the right upper limb and mandible of the claimant was NC: 2024:KHC:50808 disabled to the extent of 41%.
However, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 14%.

13. In my view, having regard to the multiple factures suffered by the claimant and having regard to the fact that he was hospitalized for more than 33 days and also had undergone multiple surgeries, it would be appropriate to treat the disability of the claimant at 20% to the whole body.
14. There is no proof of actual income of the claimant.
In such cases, since the accident is of the year 2016, the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority at Rs.9,500/- per month, would have to be adopted.

15. As the injured claimant was aged 45 years as on the date of the accident and he has suffered 20%
whole body disability, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay NC: 2024:KHC:50808 Sethi1, future prospects of 25% (Rs.2,375/-) would have to be added.

The net income would be Rs.11,875/-.
16.

Further, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma2, having regard to the fact that the claimant was aged 45 years as on the date of the accident, a multiplier of '14'
The Branch Manager vs Veluswamy on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21297794/
4 would have to be applied.

sentences.text:
17. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,99,000/- (Rs.11,875/- x 12 x '14' x 20%) towards 'loss of future income'.
18.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,10,174/-
as medical expenses on the basis of the bills that were produced.
In my view, since the medical bills were issued by Manipal Hospital which is a reputed Hospital, the Tribunal was justified in awarding the said sum and hence the same is affirmed.
National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - (2017) 16 SCC 680 Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2024:KHC:50808 19.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - (2017) 16 SCC 680 Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2024:KHC:50808 19
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has also proceeded to award a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and agony and Rs.10,000/- towards nutritious food and loss of amenities.

In my view, having regard to the multiple fractures sustained by the claimant, as stated above, and was hosptialised for more than a month, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and agony and Rs.75,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

20. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/-
towards attendant charges.
Since the claimant was hospitalized for 33 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards food, nutrition, conveyance and attendant charges.
21. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as one month.

Since the claimant was hospitalised for 33 days, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as four months and award a sum of - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:50808 Rs.38,000/- towards loss of income during the laid-up period (Rs.9,500/- x 4 months).
22.
As far as negligence is concerned, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the claimant had also contributed to the extent of 20%.

In my view, the attribution of negligence to an extent of 20%
cannot be sustained, especially when the driver of the offending motorcycle was not examined to establish that the claimant has also contributed to the accident in any manner.

23. It is also to be noticed here that the rider of the offending vehicle had in fact been charge-sheeted and this also therefore points to the fact that it was the rider of other vehicle who was responsible.
Hence
, the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard is set aside.

Consequently, the insurer of the other vehicle - 11 - The Branch Manager vs Veluswamy on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21297794/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:50808 viz., appellant in MFA No.3861 of 2018 is fastened with the entire liability of paying the compensation.

24. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be held entitled to the following compensation:
 As awarded As awarded  Sl. by the by this  Nature of Heads  No. Tribunal Court  (In Rs.) (In Rs.)
 3,99,000/-
 1. Loss of future income 1,41,120/- (Rs.11,875/- x 12 x  '14' x 20%)
 2. Pain and sufferings 10,000/- 75,000/-

3 . Medical expenses 15,10,174/- 15,10,174/-
 Loss of income during

4. 6,000/- 38,000/-
 the laid up period  5. Loss of amenities in life 10,000/- 75,000/-
 Food & nourishment  6. 40,000/-
 charges

7 . Attendant charges 5,000/-
 8. Conveyance charges Nil

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.21,37,174/- as against Rs.16,82,294/-, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum (as against 7.5%) from the date - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:50808 of petition till its realization.
However, the claimant would not be entitled for interest for the delay period of 61 days in filing the appeal.
26. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded with interest within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
27. The apportionment, deposit and release of the enhanced compensation amount shall be made as per the ratio adopted by the Tribunal.
28. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
